_comment: Every non-Python dependency the report needs, with the exact version, the public source it is
fetched from and the sha256 of that file. `setup.sh` reads this file and refuses any download
whose digest does not match. The Python environment is pinned separately in tools/requirements.txt;
the scientific packages are pinned by code_pin.yml (snapy) and tools/package-pins.json (the rest).
A digest here was taken from the file the URL served; re-record it with `bash setup.sh --print-digests`
if an upstream release is ever re-cut.

python.why: torch 2.10.0 publishes no wheel below 3.11; the report's own cards record 3.11 and 3.12 runs

tinytex.why: the workflow asks quarto-actions/setup for tinytex: true; scheme 1 carries LuaLaTeX and KOMA scrbook, and setup.sh adds the remaining packages with tlmgr
_why_tlnet_repository: Pinning the TinyTeX tarball does NOT pin TeX: scheme 1 ships no koma-script at all, so the
class the book is built on is fetched at render time from whatever the default repository
serves that day. That is a rolling mirror, and it broke the report: koma-script 3.49.3
(2026/10/19) removed \ifstr, which book/_tex/theme.tex:30 calls, and the PDF died with
on a head written four days earlier against 3.49.2.
www.texlive.info keeps a dated, immutable tlnet snapshot per day, so naming one pins every
TeX package by date the way requirements.txt pins the Python ones. 2026/10/17 is the last
snapshot before koma-script 3.49.3 and gives 3.49.2 (2026/02/02), which has \ifstr.
setup.sh runs `tlmgr update --self` against this same snapshot first, because the tlmgr in
the TinyTeX tarball is older than the snapshot's and refuses to install until it matches.
That update is deterministic: the snapshot does not move.
\ifstr is deprecated in KOMA-Script and gone from 3.49.3. Pinning buys time, it does not fix
it; book/_tex/theme.tex should move to \Ifstr, which is its chapter owner's call.

universal-ctags.why: CTAGS_VERSION of the workflow and CTAGS_VERSION of tools/code_anchors.py:50; the report's code citations are resolved with this version

_comment: snapy, pyharp and kintera configure with -DNETCDF=ON. The default route BUILDS the pinned netcdf-c
and the pinned HDF5 it sits on, and verifies that nc-config reports exactly the pinned version.
setup.sh --allow-host-netcdf is the deliberate opt-out: it links against the machine's own NetCDF,
refuses anything below `minimum`, and says that the result is not the documented route.
Preferring the host silently was the earlier behaviour and it meant the 'pinned' build was not
pinned: this host carries 4.8.1 against a 4.9.3 pin.

hdf5.why: the storage layer netcdf-c 4.9.3 sits on; built together with the pinned netcdf-c, because taking the host's HDF5 would put an unpinned library straight back underneath it

_comment: Source pins only; the shas themselves stay in their one home, so nothing here restates them.
setup.sh --with-native clones each at its pin and installs it into the virtual environment, in
this order, because each configure step finds the one before it by importing it.

pydisort.why: no pin exists for pydisort in this report; FindDisort.cmake of snapy, pyharp and kintera locates it by importing it, so it must be installed first

_why_build_differs_from_pin: These are two different questions and the report had one field for both.
`pin` is the commit the chapters CITE kintera source lines at: v2.6.2, c55b13b2. 296 citations
in 70 files resolve there, and tools/ratchet_gate.py counts any other kintera sha as `offpin`.
`build` is the commit that must be INSTALLED for the snapy commit in code_pin.yml to configure.
`find_package(Kintera 2.6.3 REQUIRED)`, so v2.6.2 cannot configure it:
Could NOT find Kintera: Found unsuitable version "2.6.2", but required is at least "2.6.3"
v2.6.3 (b6ad3739) is the smallest revision at or above that floor -- exactly one commit after
the citation pin -- so setup.sh installs that and the pinned snapy builds.
The citation pin is deliberately NOT moved here. Moving it is chapter work, not setup work:
v2.6.3 changes src/kinetics/{evaporation,kinetics}.{cpp,hpp}, and the lines shift from line 2
of evaporation.cpp onwards, so the 17 citations into those four files would silently point at
different code. Measured consequence of a bare move: ratchet offpin rises 92 -> 230 and nine
chapters fail (ch02 5->63, ch10 2->48, ch14 7->20, ch09 0->6, ch16 0->6, ch04 8->9, appa, appe,
apph). The project's own rule for the snapy pin says the same: `code_anchors.py bump` lists the
cited symbols whose body changed so their claims can be re-read. tools/check_env.py reports this
gap on every run so it stays visible until a chapter owner closes it.

pinc.why: snapy at code_pin.yml defaults PNETCDF=ON and UCX=ON on Linux (CMakeLists.txt:14-18), and PNETCDF=ON refuses to configure without this Python package: cmake/parameters.cmake:39 says "PNETCDF=ON now requires Python package 'pinc'". The report declares it nowhere, so the configure line printed in README.md stops there on a clean machine. Found by running setup.sh --with-native from a fresh clone on 2026-10-22.
